1.explanation:
• src/js/components/PageHeader/index.js: the core implementation of PageHeader—needed to see how it renders the heading and what styles or properties control text wrapping or truncation.
• src/js/components/PageHeader/stories: the Storybook examples for PageHeader, showing how the component is used with headings and parent links; reproducing the scenario uses these stories.
• src/js/components/Heading/README.md and its stories: PageHeader uses the Heading component for its title; inspecting Heading’s default wrapping, truncate, and responsive behavior helps identify whether wrapping is disabled at that level.
• src/js/components/Box/README.md: PageHeader’s layout is built with Box for alignment and spacing; knowing how Box flex and overflow are configured is essential to understand why overflow occurs.
• src/js/components/Button/README.md: the overlapping element in the screenshot is a Button; reviewing its default positioning, margin, and z-index clarifies how the overflow interacts with adjacent components.
1.bug_scenario: In the PageHeader example, a very long heading string (e.g. “LVL3928734.haiku.yosemite_34287”) does not wrap or break when it exceeds the available width. Instead, it overflows its container and collides with the adjacent “Get Started” Button, overriding the layout and pushing into the surrounding content.
